name: Self-Directed Dimension
definition: For a finite labeled set $S$, play the **labelling game** on $\mathcal H$: an adversary may first reveal any labels consistent with a member of $\mathcal H$, then the learner chooses one remaining point and a label; the adversary continues while all revealed labels remain realizable.  The **self-directed dimension** $\mathrm{SDdim}(\mathcal H)$ is the largest minimax number of learner rounds, maximized over finite $S$.  Equivalently, it is the largest depth of a realizable self-directed tree.
graph_summary: Largest depth of a realizable self-directed tree (equivalently, the labelling-game value).
description: Devulapalli and Hanneke introduced $\mathrm{SDdim}$ as a combinatorial characterization of the optimal self-directed mistake bound.  On the finite binary classes catalogued here it is exactly self-directed queries complexity.

monotonic.proof: By the established equality $\mathrm{SDdim}=\mathrm M_{\mathrm{sd}}$ and subfamily monotonicity of self-directed queries complexity.

c_monotonic.proof: By the established equality $\mathrm{SDdim}=\mathrm M_{\mathrm{sd}}$ and conditioning monotonicity of self-directed queries complexity.
